transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-11-05
Start time: 16:34 PST
Duration: 56 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marta Gomez (Aurora CTO), Samir Khan (Aurora ML Eng), Elena Park (Aurora PM)

Summary: quick scoping session to align on POC timeline and milestones. Focus areas: success criteria (latency/cost/accuracy), workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline (kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout).

Topics: kickoff, infra access (VPC, SSO), data handling/KMS, baseline benchmarks, mid-point review metrics, exec readout goals.

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, i'll kick us off. agenda is quick - align on scope and milestones for the poc.
00:18 Marta: thanks jordan, from aurora side — i'm marta, cto. main goals are reduce inference costs for our clinical summarization pipeline and hit consistent p95 latency for interactive clinician workflows.
00:32 Jordan: great, and samir/elena?
00:36 Samir: hi all, samir here. we run a hybrid pipeline - some sensitive data must stay in our VPC, others can go to hosted. curious on your private deployment options and how long setup takes.
00:49 Priya: hi, priya from redwood. we typically do a four-to-six week poc for this class of workload, kickoff, access setup, baseline benchmarks, mid-point review, then exec readout. we'll outline milestones shortly.
01:05 Elena: quick question on success criteria - for us it's a mix: quality parity with current prod (bleu/rouge not exact but clinical accuracy), latency under ~200ms p95 for short summaries, and cost per 1K requests under a target.
01:23 Jordan: makes sense; we'll capture that as acceptance criteria. can you share current qps and average tokens per request?
01:29 Samir: current peak is ~25 qps for the interactive flow, steady of 4-6 qps, average tokens per request ~120 tokens, but there are longer batch jobs up to 2k tokens.
01:45 Priya: good — that's helpful. for benchmarks we should segment into interactive path (120 tokens, 25 qps target) and batch scoring (2k tokens, lower concurrency). we'll recommend model variants and quantization profiles.
02:02 Marta: security is big for us - SOC 2, audit logs, SSO/SAML, and KMS integration for keys. can you run private control plane in our VPC?
02:15 Jordan: yes, we offer private deployment options, VPC peering or customer-managed VPC subnet. KMS/HSM integration is possible; we'll need network and key access during access setup.
02:27 Samir: also curious about caching - we have repeated prefixes in the clinical notes, can redwood do prefix or KV cache?
02:36 Priya: yes, we have prefix caching and KV cache support — sometimes the transcript tool converts K V cache to k v cash, but the runtime supports it. caching will likely help reduce cost and latency for your interactive flow.
02:50 Jordan: ok let's jump to proposed POC timeline and milestones. I'll read through and then we can adjust.
03:00 Priya: Week 0 (kickoff) — formal sign-off on scope, access list, NDA & SOC docs exchange. Week 1 — access setup: network, SSO, KMS, service accounts, sample data ingest. Week 2-3 — baseline benchmarks on your data (hosted + private if needed), tune batching/quantization/profiles. Week 4 — mid-point review: present benchmark results, performance tuning, iterate. Week 5-6 — refinement and business-level exec readout; wrap-up with go/no-go decision.
03:35 Marta: that seems reasonable. i want the mid-point review to include p95 latency, p50, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and a qualitative check on clinical accuracy with 10 canonical prompts.
03:50 Priya: we can do that. we'll run throughput tests at target concurrency, measure p50/p95/p99, and compute cost estimates from token-level accounting.
04:05 Samir: what about fallback—if the private deployment is slower, can we route to hosted for some traffic?
04:12 Jordan: yes, smart routing is part of the plan. we can route by policy (latency/cost/region) and configure automatic fallback to hosted variants during peak.
04:25 Elena: for the benchmarks, what models will you test? we currently use an L3-style open model internally, but open to suggestions.
04:34 Priya: for initial baselines we'll run two model families: a high-throughput quantized 8-bit variant and a higher-quality float16 variant. we'll also include a small redwood-verified model for comparison. names may be transcribed slightly off in notes, we'll include exact model IDs in the scope doc.
04:52 Jordan: expected deliverables at each milestone: kickoff packet, access checklist, benchmark plan, mid-point report with charts, final exec deck with recommended configuration and pricing.
05:05 Marta: can you include rollback and canary policies in the final recommendations? our platform team will want that.
05:11 Priya: yes we'll include canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies along with suggested autoscaling and burst configs.
05:22 Samir: about data retention and logs — we need audit logs for all requests and optional token redaction before persistence — can you support that?
05:33 Jordan: yes audit logs and token-level redaction is supported in private deployments. for hosted we'll discuss retention windows and redaction options too.
05:44 Marta: timeline dependencies from our side — we'll need network team to open peering, security to sign off on KMS access, and legal to complete any addenda. those are likely 3-7 business days depending on queue.
05:59 Priya: ok we'll plan slack-level coordination. who will be the point of contact for access?
06:05 Samir: i can be the technical contact for engineering + infra. elena will handle product coordination and marta will be exec sponsor.
06:15 Jordan: perfect — action items captured.

06:30 Transcript body continues with technical clarifications and small digressions (natural speech, a few overlaps):
07:00 Priya: for benchmarks, recommended baseline config: concurrency sweeps at 1, 5, 10, 25, 50; sequences at 120 and 2k; measure p50/p95/p99 and tail latency under batching enabled. we'll also test with and without prefix caching.
07:25 Samir: how do you account for tokenization differences? our current pipeline uses a slightly different tokenizer, will that skew cost?
07:33 Priya: good point — we'll normalize token counts by running our tokenization step on your sample payloads. that helps give an apples-to-apples cost estimate.
07:45 Jordan: and on the commercial side we can show expected per-1k request pricing for hosted vs dedicated reserved capacity assumptions.
07:55 Elena: can we get a mid-point readout template? execs prefer a 10-slide format with top-line delta on latency/cost/accuracy plus risk and next steps.
08:05 Priya: yes we'll provide an exec deck template.
08:12 Marta: one last security detail — we require logs forwarded to our SIEM and immutable audit trails. is forwarding supported?
08:20 Jordan: yes log forwarding & syslog/S3 ingestion supported for private deployment. for hosted we offer log export and integrations depending on plan.

08:35 Wrap-up and recap with explicit next steps:
08:40 Jordan: recap: Jordan will send POC scope and pricing doc by 2025-11-07; samir to share anonymized request logs + schema by 2025-11-10; priya to propose benchmark config by 2025-11-09; schedule kickoff week of 2025-11-12. mid-point review targeted week 4, exec readout week 5-6.
08:58 Marta: sounds good. thanks all.
09:05 Meeting end.

Notes: transcription contains typical auto-transcribe artifacts — occasional mis-spelled product names and acronyms. references to KV cache sometimes show as "K V cash" in transcript. Shared artifacts: POC scope doc (link to be sent), benchmark spreadsheet (template), SOC 2 and security whitepaper (links).
